purpose: Bracket the Chinese transcription channel with two published reconstructions instead of pretending there is one exact 328 CE pronunciation.
date_target: ca. 328 CE event; transmitted in later witnesses

sources.citation: Shimunek, Beckwith, Washington, Kontovas & Niyaz 2015, Journal Asiatique 303(1):143-151
sources.system: authors' Northern Early Middle Chinese transcription layer

sources.citation: Vovin, Vajda & de la Vaissiere 2016; reconstruction reproduced in Bonmann & Fries, Transactions of the Philological Society
sources.system: published reconstruction used for Yeniseian analysis

rows.note: Both retain s- and a high/back rounded nucleus; medial/tone notation differs.
High-value stable anchor across the two published analyses.
Aspirated dental + front diphthong broadly agrees; notation differs.
Both center on l- + front rhyme; coda/tone treatment differs.
N is normalized as velar nasal /ŋ/ for comparison.
Critical discriminator: the two published analyses reconstruct different onset/nucleus values here.
Main witnesses use 劬; later transmission also shows 助/句又-type corruption in this position.
Aspirated dental + velar stop coda broadly agrees.
N is normalized as /ŋ/; stable final nasal anchor.

guardrails: This is a lattice of published analyses, not a claim that either system is the exact spoken pronunciation in 328 CE.
Blind-fit scoring must not use the traditional Chinese glosses until the reveal pass.
谷 and the 劬/助 transmission locus must remain explicit uncertainty, not silently normalized away.
